consensus_findings.description: D7 restricts the submit-to-reconcile head advance to an exact `reconciliation_required` reply, and the D8 write matrix requires `submit` on the `pending/stay/refusal/ESCALATE` and `gate-check`/`gate-answer` rows. But `autopilot.enter_escalate` (skills/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py:496-513) sets `state.current_phase = "ESCALATE"` WITHOUT touching `total_iterations`; `total_iterations` is incremented in exactly one place, `_apply_transition` (autopilot.py:805). Every escalation therefore persists a NEW phase at the SAME transition_sequence. `submit_task` (agent-coordinator/database/migrations/035_work_queue_projection.sql:113-115) answers that exact tuple with `projection_generation_mismatch`, which D7 explicitly classifies as "other non-success envelopes remain degraded" — so the ESCALATE generation is never projected. It is not self-healing in-process either: run_loop `break`s immediately after the escalate persist (autopilot.py:1072-1073 and 1117-1118), `runner.py` gate-check exit 4 parks and the caller "must stop" (runner.py:184-188), and `gate-answer` returns 0 after enter_escalate (runner.py:244-246, 264-268, 275-278). Only a later resume-reconcile repairs it. Round-1 disposition 'Claude 1 / fixed' therefore closed the inverted-mode-mapping half of the problem while leaving the collision half open, and the required three-generation test (all produced by `_apply_transition`) will not detect it.

D5 pins the proof surface to the `/issues/list` label-only query, and proposal.md:34 accepts "within one existing kanban poll interval". That is the SPA's FALLBACK path only. `useCoordinator` (apps/kanban-viz/src/hooks/useCoordinator.ts:226-239) clears the poll interval as soon as the SSE `snapshot` event arrives, and the only incremental SSE event is `transition`, whose handler is `current.map(...)` (useCoordinator.ts:249-255) — it patches the status of cards already on the board and can never ADD a card. The backing NOTIFY is `AFTER UPDATE ON work_queue` gated on `NEW.status IN ('completed','failed','claimed','running','blocked')` (agent-coordinator/database/migrations/025_notify_enrich_change_id.sql:76-77, 113-118). A projection row INSERT (status `pending`), a reconcile cancellation (status `cancelled`), and the D9 label-only `/issues/update` all fall outside that trigger and emit nothing. So on the default connected-SSE board the newly projected phase never appears until the operator reloads or SSE errors — exactly the "kanban-viz shows no current phase" symptom proposal.md:5 says this change exists to fix. The planned tests would pass while the stated Why remains unmet. Neither package can close it as written: `agent-coordinator/database/migrations/**` is in the `deny` list of both packages (work-packages.yaml:55-56, 120-121) and wp-projection-adapter has no `agent-coordinator/**` write_allow at all.

Critical: Proposal/design/contracts assert projected `task_type=issue` rows are unclaimable by `/work/claim`, but the latest `claim_task` SQL (027_claim_task_exclude_submitter.sql) only filters `p_task_types IS NULL OR task_type = ANY(p_task_types)` with no `task_type <> 'issue'` exclusion. Python `WorkQueueService.claim` forwards that filter unchanged. `issue_service.py:5` documents the exclusion as intent, not enforcement. Pinning priority 1 (D9) makes these rows the first candidates for unfiltered claims, contradicting proposal Out of Scope (no claim-semantics change) while still advertising safety the source does not provide.

D9 asserts projection rows are "deliberately unclaimable by `/work/claim`". That is not true of the pinned contract. `claim_task` (agent-coordinator/database/migrations/027_claim_task_exclude_submitter.sql:22-24) filters only `status = 'pending' AND (p_task_types IS NULL OR task_type = ANY(p_task_types))` — there is no `task_type <> 'issue'` exclusion anywhere. `WorkQueueService.claim` passes `p_task_types` straight through (src/work_queue.py:399-409) and the MCP `get_work` tool defaults `task_types` to None (src/coordination_mcp.py:257-259), so an unfiltered claim is a reachable, in-repo call path. The docstrings that assert unclaimability (issue_service.py:4-5, coordination_mcp.py:506-507) are unenforced comments, and the round-1 disposition 'Claude 3 / fixed' adopted them as a verified property. Choosing priority 1 (D9) makes the exposure strictly worse than the default: `ORDER BY priority ASC, created_at ASC` (027:48) puts the phase-projection row ahead of every real priority-5 work item, so the FIRST unfiltered claim in a coordinated run takes the Autopilot mirror row, flips it `pending`->`claimed` (making the board render the current phase as claimed by an unrelated agent), and hands that agent a task description it cannot execute.

D7 says "an exact `reconciliation_required` response is a normal head-advance signal" without pinning where that token lives in the envelope the adapter actually receives. The bridge never surfaces it as `reason`: `_normalize_operation_response` sets `reason` only on `skipped` envelopes (coordination_bridge.py:442-460, 470-488), and a 409 falls through to the terminal `status: "error"` branch (coordination_bridge.py:509-517), which carries `status_code: 409` and puts the coordinator's problem+json body under `response`. The coordinator emits the token as `type: "urn:coordinator:work-projection:reconciliation_required"` / `detail: "reconciliation_required"` (src/coordination_api.py:843-849). An implementer reading D7 will plausibly write `result.get("reason") == "reconciliation_required"`, which never matches, silently turning head advancement into dead code that degrades on every generation past the first.

D10 requires that coordinator-free tiers "SHALL NOT import or construct the new queue-projection module", and task 1.3 makes that an import/module-spy regression. D2 simultaneously puts `project-state --mode submit|reconcile` on `runner.py`. Autopilot has no separate local-tier host — the same `runner.py` is what the sequential/local-parallel prose path shells into for `build-dispatch`, `apply-outcome`, `record-state-only-archetype`, `gate-check` and `gate-answer` (skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:72, 168, 200, 208, ...), and `runner.py` imports its dependencies at module scope today. A top-level `import queue_projection` in `runner.py` would therefore load the projection module on every local-tier CLI invocation and fail the very test task 1.3 mandates. The plan never states the import must be deferred.

Nit: Round-1 dispositions marked Claude 4 / Grok 2,7 fixed by narrowing isolation to the new projection publisher, and D10 plus the spec scenario now correctly allow pre-existing detection/archetype bridge use. proposal.md Acceptance still requires 'Coordinator-free tiers perform zero bridge imports, probes, or queue requests', and What Changes still says those tiers 'make no coordinator request'. Verified `phase_agent.py:57` eagerly imports `coordination_bridge` and archetype resolution still probes — so the proposal acceptance bar remains the unimplementable absolute that D10 retreated from.

D9's interrupted-cleanup repair is "in reconcile mode lists rows with both adapter-owned labels and clears any non-canonical leftovers", with no page size named. `IssueService.list_issues` defaults `limit=50` and hard-caps at `MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100` (agent-coordinator/src/issue_service.py:26, 288-307), and `try_issue_list` omits `limit` entirely unless the caller passes one (coordination_bridge.py:1213-1214). A long-running change whose label writes have been failing accumulates one labelled row per generation; once the backlog exceeds the page size, a single resume clears at most one page, so convergence to "exactly one active labelled projection generation" (spec.md:34) requires as many resumes as pages. The plan states the repair is retried "without changing LoopState" but never says it repeats until the leftover set is empty.

VERIFIED POSITIVE — the priority-1 / 50-row-window claim holds against real source. `IssueService.list_issues` applies `order=priority.asc,created_at.asc` and `limit` as PostgREST query parts BEFORE the fetch (issue_service.py:309-336), not as a Python post-filter, and the kanban SPA sends `{labels: ["change:<id>"]}` with no `limit`, taking the server default of 50 (apps/kanban-viz/src/hooks/useCoordinator.ts:69-76; IssueListRequest.limit=50 at coordination_api.py:254-260). A priority-1 projection row therefore sorts first and survives even with >50 ordinary priority-5 change-labelled issues, so the task-3.3 seeding proof is well-founded. The SSE snapshot builder calls the identical `list_issues(labels=[f"change:{cid}"])` (agent-coordinator/src/event_stream.py:174-184), so the filter semantics D5 tests are representative of both board paths — the divergence is in event delivery only (finding #2), not in the query.

VERIFIED POSITIVE — the two-label ownership boundary is genuinely safe against ordinary issues, and the whole-array replacement risk D9 flags is correctly bounded. `list_issues` label matching is AND at both layers (PostgREST `cs.` contains at issue_service.py:330 plus the defensive Python `all(...)` re-filter at 340-344), so requiring BOTH `change:<id>` and `projection:autopilot-phase` cannot select an ordinary change-labelled issue. Independently, `reconcile_work_projection`'s cancellation predicate keys on `input_data->>'change_id'` (035_work_queue_projection.sql:179-182), and ordinary submissions cannot set that field — both the bridge (`_validate_projection_payload`, coordination_bridge.py:745-747) and the service (`work_queue.py:711-713`) reject it as `reserved_projection_key`, and `WorkSubmitRequest` is `extra="forbid"` (coordination_api.py:216-225). So reconcile cannot collaterally cancel non-projection work for the same change. D6's allowlist plus "logs expose status/reason/task IDs but not credentials or queue payload echo" is consistent with the bridge's existing redaction posture.

VERIFIED POSITIVE — the round-1 'missing canonical writer' finding was real and D8's fix targets the right boundary. `runner.py` today exposes only `build-dispatch`, `apply-outcome`, `record-state-only-archetype`, `gate-check`, `gate-answer` (skills/autopilot/scripts/runner.py:379-482); there is no `init` and no `transition`, and `apply-outcome`'s own help text states it "NEVER modifies current_phase — the orchestrator is the sole writer of phase transitions" (runner.py:400-403). Phase advancement on the host-driven path is genuinely prose-only today, so a projection registered only in `run_loop` would never fire for the SKILL-driven runs the proposal targets. Save-failure suppression is also structurally real rather than aspirational: `persist_and_project` calls `save_state` first and lets its exception propagate before the callback is reached (autopilot.py:198-202), and `run_loop` already invokes the callback in `reconcile` mode immediately after `load_state` on resume (autopilot.py:1002-1003), matching D8's resume-before-gate ordering — the `pending_gate` early-return sits after it at autopilot.py:1027-1037.

VERIFIED POSITIVE — D9's requirement for additive coordinator-only issue list/update helpers is necessary, not defensive boilerplate. The existing `try_issue_list` and `try_issue_update` both call `_github_issue_dispatch` first and return the GitHub result whenever `github_issues.issues_backend() == "github"`, never reaching the coordinator HTTP path (coordination_bridge.py:1098-1124, 1191-1201). Reusing them for label repair would silently address GitHub issue numbers with coordinator task UUIDs. The spec's "label operations SHALL target the configured coordinator even when GitHub issues are enabled" (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:44) and the task-3.1 "GitHub-backend override resistance" case are the correct guards. `/issues/update` also supports exactly what the repair needs — whole-array `labels` replacement with no other field touched (issue_service.py:420-421, 445-450).

PACKAGE VALIDITY — checked structurally rather than by executing the validator: `openspec validate --strict` and the jsonschema check were both denied Bash approval in this session, so this is a manual read against openspec/schemas/work-packages.schema.json, not a tool result. Both packages carry every `WorkPackage` required key (package_id, task_type, description, depends_on, priority, locks, scope, worktree, timeout_minutes, retry_budget, min_trust_level, verification, outputs); top-level `schema_version`, `feature` (id + plan_revision), `contracts` (revision + openapi.primary/files) and `packages` are present; `locks` carries files+keys and `scope` carries write_allow+read_allow. Task-to-package coverage is complete and non-overlapping (1.1-2.3 -> wp-projection-adapter, 3.1-4.3 -> wp-live-integration) and the file locks match the write_allow sets. Task 4.2's runtime skill mirrors are not a scope violation: `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` are gitignored (.gitignore:280-281). Two scope notes worth confirming at implementation time: (a) if finding #2 or #3 is resolved by a migration, both packages currently `deny: agent-coordinator/database/migrations/**`; (b) wp-projection-adapter has no `agent-coordinator/**` write_allow, so any coordinator-side change must land in wp-live-integration or a third package.

In-process resume already reconciles before pending-gate handling (`autopilot.run_loop` loads state, `persist_and_project(..., mode="reconcile")`, then returns on `pending_gate`); D8/spec correctly extend the same reconcile-before-gate/work order to the host CLI protocol.

Authority, isolation, and package shape converge for the non-blocker seams: failure matrix keeps loop-state authoritative; D10/spec narrow projection isolation to the new module/helpers with import/call-spy proof; wp-live-integration no longer writes apps/kanban-viz; packages are acyclic with wp-live-integration depending on wp-projection-adapter; queue responses remain observability-only.

FYI: Acceptance still bounds board visibility to one kanban poll interval (default 5000 ms) while each projection may probe coordination then perform submit/reconcile plus label/cleanup round trips; task 4.1 documents latency but still states no numeric budget for probe reuse within one project-state invocation.

Failure matrix plus D9 partial-label/cleanup retry correctly keep save-failure suppression, projection degradation without loop-state rollback, interrupted stale-label cleanup, and idempotent resume repair as first-class behaviors; D11 bounds permanently unprojectable Autopilot change ids to one non-retrying degraded result per invocation.

Projection registration stays explicit with injected coordinator connection settings (no env-only silent enable), D6 forbids logging credentials/child transcripts/queue payload echo, and coordinator-only label helpers avoid mis-routing UUIDs into the GitHub issues backend when COORDINATION_ISSUES_BACKEND=github.

Degraded projection is required to surface bounded status/reason/task IDs without becoming authoritative, matching persist_and_project's existing non-ok envelope handling and the proposal acceptance that coordinator failure never changes loop-state.

D8 canonical write matrix and D10 projection-isolation wording are specific enough for implementers to map each runner/in-process save site and the exact helper symbols that local tiers must not call.
